rows.description: A teen who is left out finds one activity or small group built around a shared interest rather than trying to win over the popular crowd. Belonging comes more easily around doing something together.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student far from home spends nights scrolling and watching others' apparent lives. Screens numb the ache for a time but rarely give the warmth of real contact, and comparison deepens it.
graph_context: next stage: Deepening isolation and low mood
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Stage 5: Deepening isolation and low mood [Actor]
rows.description: Sleep, appetite and energy shift, and the person feels a burden and stays away from even those who care. The longer the silence, the harder reaching out feels.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Stage 5: Deepening isolation and low mood [Observer]
rows.description: A friend or hostel mate sees that someone has stopped coming out. A simple, low-pressure invitation and a steady return are better than a lecture, and persistent low mood merits a doctor or counsellor.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: The person sends a message, joins a class or says yes to a plain invitation. A small step with low stakes rebuilds the belief that contact is possible.
graph_context: next stage: Building a few real ties
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Stage 7: Building a few real ties [Response]
rows.description: Regular, modest contact such as a weekly game, a shared chore or a walk gradually grows into friendship. A few consistent bonds count more than many casual ones.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: The person sets a window for online time and pairs it with one offline plan, such as a call or a walk. Screens are kept as a tool, not a replacement for company.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child faces a test, a dog or a new class, and the stomach knots and the heart thumps. The body's alarm feels like proof that something is truly dangerous.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: The child complains of a stomach ache and stays home, and the fear drops at once. Relief teaches the brain that avoidance is the safe move, so next time the fear starts earlier.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: fear, relief, trust

rows.description: A teenager who avoided one presentation begins to dodge group chats, outings and answering the phone. The circle of safe activities shrinks and the world feels more threatening.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
